name: Bokru
title: Israelite patriarch mentioned in the genealogies
summary: Bokru is a person mentioned in the biblical genealogies in First Chronicles. He belonged to the tribe of Benjamin and is recorded as part of the family registers kept after the return from exile in Babylon. He is one of many individuals named to preserve Israel's genealogical heritage.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Bokru is listed as one of the sons of Asel in the family register for the tribe of Benjamin, as a descendant of King Saul through Jonathan.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in the parallel genealogy
keyEvents.description: The name Bokru is repeated in the parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles chapter 9, confirming his place in the tribe of Benjamin.

keyEvents.title: Part of Saul's descendants
keyEvents.description: Bokru belonged to the lineage of King Saul through Jonathan and Merib-Baal (Mephibosheth), showing that Saul's line continued to be recorded after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Preservation of genealogical records after the exile
keyEvents.description: The registration of Bokru and his family was part of the important task of restoring and preserving Israel's genealogical records after returning from the Babylonian exile.
